definition: Culture transformation deliberately changes shared habits, expectations, and norms within an organization.
example: Managers make post-incident review routine and track whether staff feel safer raising concerns.

definition: CUnit is a unit-testing framework for organizing and executing tests of C code.
example: A developer runs a suite of tests for a small C library’s boundary cases.

definition: Cured-in-place pipe is a rehabilitation method that forms a hardened lining inside an existing pipe instead of excavating its entire length.
example: A utility renews a deteriorated sewer segment from existing access points.

definition: curl is a command-line tool for transferring data to or from servers over supported network protocols.
example: A developer downloads a public dataset and records the response status.
sense_note: Distinguish the command-line program from libcurl, the underlying library.

definition: Curriculum evaluation gathers and interprets evidence to judge how well an educational program meets its goals.
example: An educator compares assessed student work with the program’s stated learning outcomes.

definition: Curriculum planning designs the sequence of learning objectives, content, experiences, and assessments for a program or course.
example: An instructor sequences prerequisite topics before assigning a capstone exercise.

definition: Customer engagement planning specifies the activities, channels, timing, and responsibilities for interacting with customers.
example: A team schedules onboarding messages and assigns owners for follow-up calls.

definition: Customer engagement strategy defines why and how an organization will build meaningful customer interactions across the relationship.
example: A business chooses to prioritize relevant support at adoption milestones over frequent generic promotions.

definition: Customer experience strategy defines the desired experience across a customer journey and coordinates changes to deliver it consistently.
example: A company brings store, delivery, and support teams together to reduce customer effort after a missed delivery.

definition: A customer insight is an actionable understanding of customer needs or behavior grounded in evidence rather than an observation alone.
example: A team learns from interviews and service data that customers abandon setup because they cannot locate required information.

definition: Customer success helps customers achieve the outcomes they intended to obtain from a product or service.
example: A customer success manager agrees on adoption goals and checks whether the customer can now complete the targeted workflow.

definition: Cutover planning and management coordinates the transition from an existing operational system to its replacement, including readiness checks and recovery arrangements.
example: A release team rehearses the switch and defines when to return to the old system if checks fail.

definition: Cyara is a platform for automated testing and monitoring of customer interactions, especially contact center and voice workflows.
example: A contact center verifies that an incoming call reaches the correct support queue.

definition: Cyber defense protects digital systems and services by reducing exposure, detecting harmful activity, and coordinating response and recovery.
example: A security team reviews access alerts and improves account protections after an incident.

definition: Cyber engineering applies engineering principles to design, validate, and maintain digital systems with defined security and resilience properties.
example: A team documents how a service isolates components and tests whether containment works under benign failure conditions.

definition: The Cyber Kill Chain is a staged conceptual model that defenders use to organize observations about intrusion activity and potential opportunities to interrupt it.
example: An incident reviewer organizes already-observed evidence by stage to identify where monitoring coverage was missing.

definition: Cyber threat hunting is the proactive review of authorized telemetry for indications of malicious activity not already surfaced by routine alerts.
example: A defender checks whether an anomalous pattern reported in one internal system also appears in other approved logs.

definition: Cyber threat intelligence turns evidence about digital threats into context that informs defensive decisions.
example: A security team assesses whether a reported threat is relevant to software the organization uses before updating priorities.

definition: Cybersecurity compliance documents and demonstrates that security controls satisfy applicable policies, regulations, or standards.
example: A control owner collects evidence that restricted account access is regularly reviewed.

definition: D3.js is a JavaScript library for binding data to web elements and building customized interactive visualizations.
example: A developer binds incident counts to map features and updates colors as a filter changes.

definition: Dagger 2 is a compile-time dependency injection framework for Java applications, including Android projects.
example: A build checks whether all objects required by a feature can be provided by its dependency graph.

definition: DALL·E is a family of generative image models that create visual outputs from text prompts or related inputs.
example: An artist requests several conceptual images for preliminary composition review.

definition: Darik’s Boot and Nuke was a bootable utility designed to overwrite supported computer storage media for data erasure.
example: An asset-disposal reviewer checks a historical record of an authorized disk wipe and its verification.
sense_note: Do not assume erasure suitability for other media, especially solid-state devices.

definition: dashDB was IBM’s name for a database service oriented toward analytical workloads and data warehousing.
example: A data analyst runs aggregate queries on a historical dashDB data warehouse.
sense_note: Verify the exact legacy offering when present-day product identity matters.

definition: Data center cooling manages heat and environmental conditions so computing equipment operates within intended ranges.
example: A facilities team compares inlet temperatures across racks to identify a cooling imbalance.

definition: Data center design plans the computing facility and its power, cooling, connectivity, physical layout, and resilience requirements.
example: A design team evaluates whether a proposed equipment layout can meet both power and heat loads.

definition: Data center facility management operates and maintains the building services that support a data center’s computing infrastructure.
example: A facilities manager schedules preventive maintenance of backup power and cooling equipment.

definition: Data center operations keeps the facility’s computing and supporting systems running through monitoring, maintenance, incident response, and planned change.
example: An operator coordinates hardware replacement with service owners to minimize downtime.

definition: Data classification assigns data to categories according to its content, sensitivity, or business and handling requirements.
example: A records team marks payment records as restricted so additional handling controls apply.

definition: Data deduplication identifies and removes or consolidates redundant copies of data while preserving needed information.
example: A storage system records identical file blocks once and points multiple files to the stored copy.

definition: Data-driven decision-making uses relevant evidence and analysis to inform judgment about what action to take.
example: A library compares attendance records and reader feedback before changing its opening hours.

definition: Data-driven instruction uses evidence of learner progress or difficulty to adjust what is taught and how it is taught.
example: A teacher reteaches fractions after reviewing errors common across a class’s recent assessments.

definition: Data-driven manufacturing uses operational data and analysis to guide production, quality, or maintenance decisions.
example: A plant investigates increasing scrap rates using measurements linked to production shifts.

definition: Data engineering designs and maintains systems that reliably ingest, transform, store, and serve data.
example: An engineer builds a pipeline that checks incoming sales records and makes validated data available for reporting.

definition: Alphanumeric data entry accurately inputs records containing letters, numbers, and sometimes symbols into a system.
example: A clerk transcribes product identifiers containing both letters and digits and verifies each against the source.

definition: Numeric data entry accurately inputs data such as amounts, counts, and measured values into a system.
example: A clerk enters invoice amounts and checks that the decimal places match the source records.

definition: Data modeling represents entities, attributes, and relationships or other structures that determine how information is organized and used.
example: A designer models orders and line items separately so each order can contain multiple products.

definition: A data pipeline is a sequence of connected processes that moves data between systems and may validate, transform, or enrich it along the way.
example: A scheduled pipeline reads new records, standardizes dates, and writes validated data to an analytics table.

definition: Data Vault modeling structures a data warehouse around hubs for business keys, links for relationships, and satellites for descriptive history.
example: A warehouse stores supplier identifiers in a hub and records changing supplier attributes in a satellite.

definition: Data visualization represents data visually to help people inspect patterns, comparisons, distributions, or relationships.
example: An analyst plots a distribution rather than showing only an average so readers can see outliers.
